name: Queen's Gambit (as White)
desc: White offers the c-pawn to deflect Black's d5 pawn and dominate the center. A complete repertoire against everything: QGD, QGA, Slav, Semi-Slav, Tarrasch, Chigorin, Albin and Baltic, including the classic traps.

lines.name: QGD Orthodox 4...Be7
lines.moves: 1.d4 {Taking the center with a protected pawn.} d5 2.c4 {The Queen's Gambit: challenging d5 from the side.} e6 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Bg5 {Pinning the knight and increasing pressure on d5.} Be7 5.e3 O-O 6.Nf3 Nbd7 7.Rc1 {Pressure on the c-file.} c6 8.Bd3 dxc4 9.Bxc4 Nd5 10.Bxe7 Qxe7 11.O-O Nxc3 12.Rxc3 {Capablanca's freeing maneuver; White keeps a pleasant edge.}

lines.name: QGD Cambridge Springs
lines.moves: 1.d4 d5 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Bg5 Nbd7 5.e3 {Don't fall for 5.cxd5 exd5 6.Nxd5?? Nxd5! — the Elephant Trap.} c6 6.Nf3 Qa5 {The Cambridge Springs: pinning the c3 knight.} 7.Nd2 {Unpinning and covering c4.}

lines.name: QGD 3...Be7
lines.moves: 1.d4 d5 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Be7 4.Nf3 Nf6 5.Bf4 {The modern Bf4 system.} O-O 6.e3 c5 7.dxc5 Bxc5 8.Qc2 Nc6 9.a3 {Solid and flexible.}

lines.name: Tarrasch Defense 3...c5
lines.moves: 1.d4 d5 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 c5 {The Tarrasch: accepting an isolated pawn for activity.} 4.cxd5 exd5 5.Nf3 Nc6 6.g3 {The Rubinstein system: bishop to g2 against d5.} Nf6 7.Bg2 Be7 8.O-O O-O 9.Bg5 {Targeting the isolated pawn.}

lines.name: QGA 3.e3
lines.moves: 1.d4 d5 2.c4 dxc4 {Queen's Gambit Accepted.} 3.e3 {Preparing Bxc4.} Nf6 4.Bxc4 e6 5.Nf3 c5 6.O-O a6 7.a4 {Stopping ...b5.} Nc6 8.Qe2 cxd4 9.Rd1 {Classical QGA: White regains d4 with active pieces.}

lines.name: QGA trap 3...b5?
lines.moves: 1.d4 d5 2.c4 dxc4 3.e3 b5? {Trying to hold the pawn.} 4.a4 c6 5.axb5 cxb5 6.Qf3 {The queen forks a8 along the long diagonal: Black loses material.}

lines.name: QGA 3...e5
lines.moves: 1.d4 d5 2.c4 dxc4 3.e3 e5 4.Bxc4 exd4 5.exd4 Nf6 6.Nf3 Be7 7.O-O O-O 8.h3 {An isolated pawn but active pieces.}

lines.name: Slav Defense
lines.moves: 1.d4 d5 2.c4 c6 {The Slav: supporting d5 without blocking the bishop.} 3.Nf3 Nf6 4.Nc3 dxc4 5.a4 {Stopping ...b5.} Bf5 6.e3 e6 7.Bxc4 Bb4 8.O-O O-O 9.Qe2 {Preparing e4.}

lines.name: Semi-Slav
lines.moves: 1.d4 d5 2.c4 c6 3.Nf3 Nf6 4.Nc3 e6 {The Semi-Slav.} 5.e3 Nbd7 6.Qc2 Bd6 7.Bd3 O-O 8.O-O dxc4 9.Bxc4 {White plans e4.}

lines.name: Chigorin Defense 2...Nc6
lines.moves: 1.d4 d5 2.c4 Nc6 {The Chigorin: piece play over structure.} 3.Nf3 Bg4 4.cxd5 Bxf3 5.gxf3 Qxd5 6.e3 e5 7.Nc3 Bb4 8.Bd2 Bxc3 9.bxc3 {White has the bishop pair.}

lines.name: Albin Countergambit 2...e5
lines.moves: 1.d4 d5 2.c4 e5 {The Albin Countergambit.} 3.dxe5 d4 4.Nf3 {Never 4.e3? Bb4+ 5.Bd2 dxe3! — the Lasker Trap.} Nc6 5.g3 Be6 6.Nbd2 Qd7 7.Bg2 O-O-O 8.O-O {Main line: White's king is safer.}

lines.name: Baltic Defense 2...Bf5
lines.moves: 1.d4 d5 2.c4 Bf5 {The Baltic Defense.} 3.cxd5 Bxb1 4.Rxb1 Qxd5 5.a3 {White has the bishop pair and will gain time with Nf3, e3 and Nc3 ideas.}

name: London System
desc: A reliable system: Bf4, e3, Nf3, c3, Nbd2 and Bd3 against almost anything. Easy to learn, but you must know the sharp ...c5 and ...Qb6 tries and the b2 poisoned pawn tricks.

lines.name: Main setup vs ...d5
lines.moves: 1.d4 d5 2.Bf4 {The London: bishop out before e3.} Nf6 3.e3 e6 4.Nf3 c5 5.c3 {The classic London pyramid.} Nc6 6.Nbd2 Bd6 7.Bg3 {Keeping the bishop and inviting ...Bxg3 hxg3 with an open h-file.} O-O 8.Bd3 {Perfect setup.}

lines.name: Early ...c5 and ...Qb6
lines.moves: 1.d4 d5 2.Bf4 c5 3.e3 Nc6 4.c3 Qb6 {Hitting b2.} 5.Qb3 {Defending b2 by offering a queen trade.} c4 6.Qc2 Bf5 7.Qc1 {Unusual but standard: the queen protects b2 and will reroute.}

lines.name: Symmetrical 2...Bf5
lines.moves: 1.d4 d5 2.Bf4 Bf5 3.e3 e6 4.c4 {Exploiting the absence of Black's bishop from the queenside.} Bb4+ 5.Nc3 Nf6 6.Qb3 {Hitting b7 and the b4 bishop.}

lines.name: Early blunder 2...e5?
lines.moves: 1.d4 d5 2.Bf4 e5? {A premature break.} 3.dxe5 Nc6 4.Nf3 {A clean extra pawn.}

lines.name: vs King's Indian setup
lines.moves: 1.d4 Nf6 2.Bf4 g6 3.e3 Bg7 4.Nf3 O-O 5.Be2 d6 6.h3 {A luft for the bishop.} Nbd7 7.O-O {Solid and simple.}

lines.name: vs ...c5 Qb6: b2 is poisoned
lines.moves: 1.d4 Nf6 2.Bf4 c5 3.e3 Qb6 4.Nc3 {The b2 pawn is poisoned: 4...Qxb2? 5.Nb5! threatens Nc7+.} Qxb2? 5.Nb5 {Threatening Nc7+ and Rb1: Black's queen is in danger.}

lines.name: vs ...c5 cxd4
lines.moves: 1.d4 Nf6 2.Bf4 c5 3.e3 cxd4 4.exd4 d5 5.c3 Nc6 6.Nf3 Bg4 7.Nbd2 {A Caro-Kann Exchange with colours reversed.}

lines.name: vs Dutch 1...f5
lines.moves: 1.d4 f5 2.Bf4 Nf6 3.e3 e6 4.Nf3 b6 5.h3 Bb7 6.Nbd2 {Control of e5 and a sound structure.}

name: English Opening
desc: White grabs d5 from the flank with 1.c4 and usually fianchettoes the king's bishop. Learn the Reversed Sicilian, the Symmetrical English, the Botvinnik setup and answers to early ...d5 and ...e6.

lines.name: Reversed Sicilian 1...e5
lines.moves: 1.c4 {The English: controlling d5.} e5 2.Nc3 Nf6 3.Nf3 Nc6 4.g3 d5 5.cxd5 Nxd5 6.Bg2 {A reversed Dragon with an extra tempo.} Nb6 7.O-O Be7 8.d3 O-O 9.a3 {Preparing b4.}

lines.name: Botvinnik setup vs ...g6
lines.moves: 1.c4 e5 2.Nc3 Nc6 3.g3 g6 4.Bg2 Bg7 5.d3 d6 6.Nf3 f5 7.O-O Nf6 8.Rb1 {Preparing the b4-b5 queenside expansion.}

lines.name: Symmetrical 1...c5
lines.moves: 1.c4 c5 {The Symmetrical English.} 2.Nc3 Nc6 3.g3 g6 4.Bg2 Bg7 5.Nf3 Nf6 6.O-O O-O 7.d4 {Opening the center.} cxd4 8.Nxd4 {More active pieces.}

lines.name: 1...Nf6 King's Indian setup
lines.moves: 1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 g6 3.e4 {Grabbing the center.} d6 4.d4 Bg7 5.Be2 O-O 6.Nf3 e5 7.O-O Nc6 8.d5 {Gaining space.}

lines.name: 1...e6 Reti style
lines.moves: 1.c4 e6 2.Nf3 d5 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 Be7 5.O-O O-O 6.b3 {Double fianchetto.} c5 7.Bb2 {Both bishops rake the center.}

lines.name: 1...d5?! early center
lines.moves: 1.c4 d5?! 2.cxd5 Qxd5 3.Nc3 {Gaining time on the queen.} Qd8 4.d4 Nf6 5.e4 {A big classical center.}

name: Catalan Opening
desc: A blend of the Queen's Gambit and the Réti: the bishop on g2 puts long-term pressure on the queenside. Learn the Open and Closed Catalan and how to deal with ...Bb4+ and ...c5.

lines.name: Open Catalan 4...dxc4
lines.moves: 1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 e6 3.g3 {The Catalan.} d5 4.Bg2 dxc4 {The Open Catalan.} 5.Qa4+ {Regaining the pawn quickly.} Bd7 6.Qxc4 Bc6 7.Nf3 Bd5 8.Qd3 c5 9.Nc3 Bc6 10.O-O {White has a pleasant lead in development.}

lines.name: Closed Catalan 4...Be7
lines.moves: 1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 e6 3.g3 d5 4.Bg2 Be7 5.Nf3 O-O 6.O-O Nbd7 7.Qc2 c6 8.Nbd2 b6 9.e4 {The thematic central break.}

lines.name: 3...Bb4+
lines.moves: 1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Bb4+ 4.Bd2 Be7 5.Bg2 d5 6.Nf3 O-O 7.O-O {Back to a Catalan with the bishop usefully on d2.}

lines.name: 3...c5 Benoni style
lines.moves: 1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 e6 3.g3 c5 4.d5 exd5 5.cxd5 d6 6.Nc3 g6 7.Bg2 Bg7 8.Nf3 O-O 9.O-O {A Fianchetto Benoni: White's bishop fits perfectly.}

name: Queen's Gambit Declined (as Black)
desc: The classical, rock-solid answer to 1.d4. Learn the Tartakower against 4.Bg5, the Carlsbad structure in the Exchange, the 5.Bf4 system and the Catalan setups.

lines.name: Tartakower vs 4.Bg5
lines.moves: 1.d4 d5 2.c4 e6 {Declining: keeping a firm grip on d5.} 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Bg5 Be7 5.e3 O-O 6.Nf3 h6 7.Bh4 b6 {The Tartakower: fianchettoing the problem bishop.} 8.Be2 Bb7 9.Bxf6 Bxf6 10.cxd5 exd5 {Solid with the bishop pair.}

lines.name: Exchange Variation
lines.moves: 1.d4 d5 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.cxd5 exd5 5.Bg5 c6 6.Qc2 Be7 7.e3 Nbd7 8.Bd3 O-O 9.Nge2 Re8 {The Carlsbad structure: Black aims for ...Nf8 and kingside play.}

lines.name: 5.Bf4 system
lines.moves: 1.d4 d5 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Nf3 Be7 5.Bf4 O-O 6.e3 c5 7.dxc5 Bxc5 8.Qc2 Nc6 9.a3 Qa5 {Active counterplay.}

lines.name: Catalan 3.Nf3 4.g3
lines.moves: 1.d4 d5 2.c4 e6 3.Nf3 Nf6 4.g3 Be7 5.Bg2 O-O 6.O-O dxc4 7.Qc2 a6 8.Qxc4 b5 9.Qc2 Bb7 {The Open Catalan: Black challenges the g2 bishop.}

name: Slav Defense (as Black)
desc: Black defends d5 with ...c6, keeping the c8 bishop free. Learn the main line with 5...Bf5, the Exchange Slav, the 4.e3 and Nh4 plans, and the Meran-style Semi-Slav.

lines.name: Main line 5...Bf5
lines.moves: 1.d4 d5 2.c4 c6 {The Slav.} 3.Nf3 Nf6 4.Nc3 dxc4 5.a4 Bf5 {The bishop gets out.} 6.e3 e6 7.Bxc4 Bb4 8.O-O Nbd7 9.Qe2 O-O 10.e4 Bg6 {Solid main line.}

lines.name: Exchange Slav
lines.moves: 1.d4 d5 2.c4 c6 3.cxd5 cxd5 4.Nc3 Nf6 5.Bf4 Nc6 6.e3 Bf5 7.Nf3 e6 8.Qb3 Bb4 {Equal and symmetrical.}

lines.name: 4.e3 Bf5 5.Nh4
lines.moves: 1.d4 d5 2.c4 c6 3.Nf3 Nf6 4.e3 Bf5 5.Nc3 e6 6.Nh4 Bg6 7.Nxg6 hxg6 {The open h-file compensates for the bishop pair.}

lines.name: Geller Gambit 5.e4!?
lines.moves: 1.d4 d5 2.c4 c6 3.Nf3 Nf6 4.Nc3 dxc4 5.e4!? {A sharp gambit.} b5 {Holding the pawn.} 6.e5 Nd5 7.a4 e6 8.axb5 Nxc3 9.bxc3 cxb5 10.Ng5 Bb7 {Black holds the extra pawn.}

lines.name: 3.Nc3 Meran style
lines.moves: 1.d4 d5 2.c4 c6 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.e3 e6 5.Nf3 Nbd7 6.Bd3 dxc4 7.Bxc4 b5 {The Meran.} 8.Bd3 Bb7 {Preparing ...a6 and ...c5.}

name: Albin Countergambit (as Black)
desc: An aggressive answer to the Queen's Gambit: Black sacrifices a pawn for a cramping d4 wedge. Includes the famous Lasker Trap with an underpromotion to a knight!

lines.name: Main line 5.g3
lines.moves: 1.d4 d5 2.c4 e5 {The Albin Countergambit.} 3.dxe5 d4 {A powerful wedge in White's camp.} 4.Nf3 Nc6 5.g3 Be6 6.Nbd2 Qd7 {Preparing queenside castling.} 7.Bg2 O-O-O {Opposite-side castling with attacking chances.}

lines.name: Lasker Trap 4.e3?
lines.moves: 1.d4 d5 2.c4 e5 3.dxe5 d4 4.e3? {Natural but a mistake.} Bb4+ 5.Bd2 dxe3! 6.Bxb4?? exf2+ 7.Ke2 fxg1=N+! {The Lasker Trap: an underpromotion to a knight with check!} 8.Ke1 Qh4+ {Black is winning.}

lines.name: 4.Nf3 Nc6 5.Nbd2
lines.moves: 1.d4 d5 2.c4 e5 3.dxe5 d4 4.Nf3 Nc6 5.Nbd2 Be6 6.g3 Qd7 7.Bg2 O-O-O {Same plan: castle long and attack.}
